newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA'S DISMAL FORM DAMPENS CELEBRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA'S DISMAL FORM DAMPENS CELEBRATIONS.

text.p: Amid the euphoria surrounding West Indies' emphatic victory over Australia in the third test on Saturday, the world's most celebrated batsman stands alone in a personal crisis of confidence.
Brian Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first class cricket, is enduring a dismal tour of Australia, adding a further twist to his increasingly chequered career.

Having already been dropped one place down the order to number four because of his form slump, Lara scored two in both innings as the tourists inflicted a six-wicket defeat on Mark Taylor's side inside three days at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
But his captain, Courtney Walsh, retains his faith in Lara, saying the left-hander is simply trying too hard.
"I don't think there is anything wrong with him mentally. It's just that his confidence is down and he is trying too hard," Walsh said.
"I have seen him down before but not out. He's not started well on other tours before but he's managed to come back."
Lara, who fell out badly with West Indian cricket officials after being fined for poor behaviour last year, has amassed a paltry seven runs in his last four test innings.
In three test matches against Australia, the newly-appointed vice-captain has scored just 77 runs, losing his wicket to fast bowler Glenn McGrath on five occasions.
But it was the nature of his dismissals in Melbourne that most dismayed West Indies supporters.
In both innings, Lara played a rash back foot drive to a wide delivery only to be caught in the gully area.
"Brian wants to contribute to the team and he feels he is not doing that but he is determined to come good," Walsh said.
The veteran fast bowler said he was trying everything he could to ease Lara out of his current slump.
"I'm just trying to get him more relaxed. He is so keyed up and wants to do so well that he is just trying a little too hard," Walsh said.
